lines.text: In April 2021, Parker Solar Probe flew into the Sun's atmosphere.
It stayed inside for about five hours, thirteen million kilometres above the Sun's visible surface.
The surface is about five thousand five hundred degrees Celsius. The atmosphere above it reaches up to two million.
Behind its heat shield, the instruments stayed at eighty-five degrees Fahrenheit. That's about thirty Celsius.
So how did it stay that cool? The full video on our channel has the answer. Like and subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
